text.p: A Ronaldo hat-trick helped Barcelona to an exciting 5-2 victory at Atletico Madrid on Sunday and ensured that the Catalan side remained second in the Spanish championship.
Leaders Real Madrid, comfortable 2-0 winners over Logrones earlier, maintained their seven-point lead with nine games left.
Barcelona had started needing a result because Real Betis took provisional second place after snatching an injury time winner at Real Sociedad.
The situation looked bad for Bobby Robson's side after Kiko Narvaez controlled a pass from Diego Simeone and scooped a fine lob over keeper Vitor Baia on 15 minutes.
But Barcelona turned the game around in the five minutes before halftime thanks to Ivan de la Pena.

The shaven-headed midfielder curled in a superb free-kick to equalise in the 40th minute, and shortly afterwards put through Ronaldo, who was aided by a slip by defender Daniel Prodan and saw his shot bounce in off the far post.
But luck was against the Brazilian moments later, when he was denied by the other post after breaking free from a badly-shaken Atletico defence.
Ronaldo seemed to put the game beyond Atletico's reach on the hour when he burst through and rounded keeper Jose Molina.
But the home side struck straight back when Kiko broke through and rammed home the rebound after his first shot was saved by Baia.

Moments later the home fans saw their hopes dashed when Diego Simeone was sent off for an ugly challenge on Luis Figo, and Atletico were reduced to nine 15 minutes from time when Santi Denia brought down Figo in the area.
Ronaldo completed his hat-trick from the spot, and could have had a fourth two minutes from time when he broke free and passed to Figo to score with just Molina to beat.
"We're getting better game by game," said Ronaldo after the match, which was the last of an extraordinary series of encounters between the two sides this season.
The saga included a 6-5 aggregate victory for Barcelona in the Spanish Super Cup, a 3-3 league draw and a memorable Barcelona comeback from 3-0 down to win 5-4 in the Spanish Cup quarter-finals.
Real Madrid, by contrast, continue to play with more effectiveness than flair.
They went ahead in the first half when Victor Sanchez pounced on an error in the Logrones defence, and Raul Gonzalez took advantage of another blunder to wrap up the game after the break.
Zaragoza climbed out of danger with a 2-0 home win over Hercules, while surprise outfit Valladolid continued their UEFA Cup challenge with a 2-1 win at Sporting Gijon which leaft them sixth.
